claims.text: Adding 2–5 mol% Hf to ZrB2 precursor powders can produce a homogeneous (Zr1−xHfx)B2 solid solution.
Rigorous pre-sintering homogenization will ensure uniform Hf distribution.
Hf is isomorphous with Zr in the proposed diboride system.
Uniformly distributed Hf lowers the activation energy for grain-boundary diffusion in ZrB2.
Lower grain-boundary diffusion activation energy enhances densification.
The Hf-modified material can achieve full densification at approximately 2100 °C.
The proposed Hf modification reduces the required sintering temperature relative to the conventional process above 2300 °C.
Hf doping and homogenization produce a microstructure with minimal or significantly reduced residual porosity.
The resulting grain boundaries are stronger than those in conventionally prepared ZrB2.
Less porous grain boundaries better withstand chemical attack from a liquid plating bath.
Less porous grain boundaries better withstand thermal stresses during prolonged liquid plating bath exposure.
The Hf-doped material will show less hole formation during at least 72 hours of liquid plating bath exposure than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
The Hf-doped material will show less crack initiation during at least 72 hours of liquid plating bath exposure than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C typically has higher porosity than the proposed Hf-doped material.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 is more susceptible to hole and crack formation during prolonged liquid plating bath exposure.
Spark plasma sintering or hot pressing in an inert atmosphere at approximately 2100 °C is the proposed preparation route for the Hf-doped material.
Performance outside liquid plating bath exposures of at least 72 hours at the nominal operating temperature is uncertain.
